summary: Self-hosted Actions runner heartbeat drops and token refresh failures concurrent with Vault transit key rotation
description: Issue summary: Several self-hosted GitHub Actions runners in the us-west pool lost regular heartbeat and began failing job token refreshes during a scheduled Vault transit key rotation. Impact: Multiple release and CI jobs timed out or failed to acquire temporary credentials, blocking canary deployments and a night-time release window. Environment: Production, self-hosted GitHub Actions runners (us-west autoscaled pool) behind bastion-proxy-01, Vault 1.12 with transit backend, runner fleet image: rwi-runner:2026.02.18.
impact: ~30% of CI job runs in the us-west pool failed or timed out over a 45-minute window; release pipeline for v2.14 stalled; on-call SRE escalation opened.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger scheduled Vault transit key rotation (staged rollout used). 2) Observe runner manager performing cert/key rewrap operations. 3) Run long-lived workflow that refreshes GitHub Actions runner token mid-job. 4) Note intermittent token refresh failures and runner heartbeat gap events in runner-manager logs.
observed_behavior: Runners dropped heartbeat for 20-35s, systemd shows transient cgroups latency spikes, runner-manager emitted 401s when calling /_token/refresh proxy endpoints, and Vault audit logs show a burst of transit/decrypt requests failing with 'request timed out' from a handful of runner IPs.
expected_behavior: Key rotation should not disrupt in-flight token refresh operations or cause heartbeat gaps beyond a few seconds; runners should transparently rewrap with new transit key or fall back to cached key until rotation completes.
logs_and_artifacts: - /var/log/runner-manager.log excerpts (attached) - Vault audit snippets: 2026-03-09T03:12:24Z transit/decrypt timeout for cidr 10.42.5.0/24 - systemd-journal: cgroup reclaim delays observed concurrent with SSH multiplexing reconnects - GitHub Actions runner worker logs: 'token refresh failed: 401 unauthorized' lines around 03:12-03:30 UTC.
investigation_notes: 03/09 03:15 - On-call SRE (Marco) confirmed correlation between Vault transit key rotation window and start of failures.
03/09 03:22 - Observed that bastion-proxy-01 had increased TCP retransmits during rotation; packet capture shows symmetric retransmit spikes to Vault cluster nodes.

03/09 03:30 - Hypothesis: rotation triggered synchronous re-encryption calls from many runners causing a brief thundering herd against Vault transit and transient networking saturation on the bastion path.
03/10 09:05 - Replayed operations in staging: rotation with staggered clients avoided failures; immediate mitigation reduces concurrency on rewrap calls.
03/12 14:40 - Found runner-manager logic performs immediate synchronous rewrap on first request post-rotation; change to async lazy-rewrap prepared as patch (branch: infra/runners/async-rewrap).
03/12 16:55 - Identified a secondary issue: token refresh proxy retries were too aggressive (0 backoff), amplifying load; proposed changes to introduce exponential backoff and circuit breaker.
03/13 10:12 - Confirmed Vault cluster CPU briefly hit 85% during rotation due to decrypt rewrap work; increasing transit worker threads only partially mitigated the spike.
temporary_workaround: 1) Rolled back to using previous transit key for in-flight sessions via feature flag on runner-manager for 2 hours to clear job backlog. 2) Throttled runner-manager rewrap concurrency at the bastion level (iptables hashlimit) until patch merged.
fix_plan: 1) Merge infra/runners/async-rewrap to make rewraps lazy and nonblocking. 2) Add exponential backoff and a circuit breaker to token refresh proxy. 3) Update rotation playbook to pre-warm transit worker pool and stagger rewrap windows across runner pools. 4) Post-deploy monitoring: add a 'rotation storm' alert set (Vault transit API error rate + bastion retransmit rate) with a 1-minute window.
resolution_notes: In-progress: patch for async lazy rewrap queued (PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-ops/pull/198); planned rollout to canary pool 2026-03-15. Operational runbook updated with staggered rewrap recommendation. No long-term data loss; CI backlog cleared after temporary workaround.
next_steps: - Code review and merge PR for async rewrap and token-proxy backoff (owner: Marco). - Schedule canary rollout during low-traffic window and monitor runner heartbeats and Vault audit logs. - Follow-up postmortem to be authored after stability window (owner: Priya).
comments: Priya Patel (2026-03-09): Filed after initial on-call handoff. Noticed multiple release jobs stuck in "waiting-for-runner" state; attaching job ids and logs.
Marco Delgado (2026-03-09): Confirmed correlation with Vault rotation. Spiking decrypt ops and bastion retransmits. Investigating whether the proxy retries amplify load.
Ellen Zhao (SRE) (2026-03-10): Deployed temporary iptables throttling on bastion-proxy-01 which reduced retransmit rate ~60%. Suggest adding a quota for rewrap per-second per-client.
Marco Delgado (2026-03-12): Prepared a candidate patch to make rewraps async (branch infra/runners/async-rewrap). Testing in staging now.
Priya Patel (2026-03-13): Will own postmortem drafts and coordinate release engineers for canary schedule. Leaving ticket open until PR is in prod and 48h stable.

Security (Ravi Menon) (2026-03-13): Reviewed temporary workaround. Confirmed reusing previous transit key for in-flight sessions is acceptable for short windows, documented exception in rotation checklist.
